## Overview

CoreWeave reported record third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.661 billion, a significant acceleration from $1.365 billion in the same period of 2025. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=20] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=22] --> The company characterized the quarter as a "breakout quarter" driven by disciplined growth at scale and expanding margins. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=7] -->

Financial results were supported by diverse funding sources, including financing backed by customer contracts, operating cash flow, and approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] --> This liquidity position underpins the company’s ability to fund continued infrastructure buildout during its rapid expansion phase. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

## Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**1. Demand Momentum: 4/5**

Revenue growth is robust, with Q3 2026 revenue of $3.661 billion increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially from the prior quarter. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] --> Year-over-year revenue growth stands at approximately 168%, rising from $1.365 billion in Q3 2025 to $3.661 billion in Q3 2026. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=22] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=20] --> The backlog of demand is further evidenced by approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months, indicating strong forward-looking commitment. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

**2. Expansion Capacity: 4/5**

The company’s growth is supported by multiple sources of funding, including financing backed by customer contracts, which allows for continued infrastructure buildout. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] --> Operating cash flow also contributes to the capital flexibility needed to scale AI infrastructure. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] --> The mention of "financing backed by customer contracts" suggests a model where capacity expansion is directly tied to secured revenue streams, reducing the risk of building unutilized assets. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

**3. Strategic Durability: 3/5**

Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 62% in Q3 2026 from 61% in Q3 2025, demonstrating operating leverage at scale. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=72] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=74] --> However, GAAP operating income margin improved only slightly to 6% from 4%, and the company still reported a net loss of $709 million, highlighting the heavy capital and interest expense burden associated with its model. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=32] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=34] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=43] --> The dependence on large prepayments and customer-backed financing, while strong for short-term liquidity, introduces structural risk if customer AI adoption or funding willingness shifts. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

## Valuation Insights

Fiscal 2025 revenue grew 167.9% to $5,131 million, but operating income swung from a $324 million profit in fiscal 2024 to a $46 million loss in fiscal 2025. <!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=5131000000;1915000000|result=1.6794|definition=revenue growth] --> The resulting operating margin is -0.9% in fiscal 2025, a sharp deterioration from the 16.9% margin achieved in fiscal 2024. <!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=-46000000;5131000000|result=-0.009|definition=operating income / total revenue] -->

Cash from operations increased to $3,058 million in fiscal 2025, but capital expenditures of $10,309 million produced negative free cash flow of $(7,251) million. <!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities|period=2025-01-01:2025-12-31|value=3058000000] --> Total debt rose from $7,926 million to $21,373 million in 2025, raising the debt-to-equity ratio to 6.41x versus 1.92x in the prior period. <!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent|period=2025-12-31|value=14665000000] -->

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

CoreWeave’s immediate future is anchored by the expected inflow of approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits within the next three months, which provides substantial visibility into near-term revenue and capital deployment. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] --> The company’s strategy to "keep delivering the infrastructure and software customers need to build, run, and scale AI" suggests a focus on vertical integration to capture more value in the AI stack. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

A key strategic recommendation is for CoreWeave to accelerate the conversion of its large prepayment base into recurring operating revenue while managing its high interest expense, which reached $846 million in Q3 2026. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=38] --> Given the net loss margin of (19)%, the company must continue to demonstrate that its adjusted EBITDA profitability can transition into GAAP profitability to sustain investor confidence. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=47] --> <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=72] --> The firm should also monitor competitive pressure in the AI infrastructure market, as its growth currently relies heavily on securing and executing on large-scale customer contracts. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

Insight: CoreWeave’s interest expense, net, more than tripled year-over-year from $310 million to $846 million, a level that significantly outpaced the growth in operating income, which rose from $52 million to $207 million. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=38] -->

## Investment Recommendation

Rating: Hold. CoreWeave demonstrates exceptional top-line momentum, with Q3 2026 revenue of $3.661 billion, a 168% year-over-year increase from $1.365 billion. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=20] --> This growth is underpinned by approximately $9 billion in expected customer prepayments, providing near-term visibility. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=12] -->

The decisive risk is the explosive debt burden; total debt rose from $7,926 million to $21,373 million in 2025, driving a debt-to-equity ratio to 6.41x. <!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent|period=2025-12-31|value=14665000000] --> While Q3 2026 operating income improved to $207 million, it remains overwhelmed by $846 million in interest expense, favoring patience over aggressive accumulation. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=38] -->

Insight: CoreWeave’s interest expense, net, more than tripled year-over-year from $310 million to $846 million, a level that significantly outpaced the growth in operating income, which rose from $52 million to $207 million. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=38] -->

Insight: Third quarter 2026 GAAP operating income was $207 million, a 298% increase over the $52 million reported in the same quarter of 2025. <!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=28] -->
